title: Which enlarged tiger picture is proportional to the first?
description: Two enlarged copies of the tiger picture are compared with the first one. The video finds the factor of change for the width and for the height of each copy and sets the two side by side. Keeko's doubt is that a copy whose sides grew by different lengths cannot be proportional.
teaching_notes: One idea: a change is proportional when the width and the height are multiplied by the same factor, even if they grow by different lengths. Watch for students who compare how much was added instead of the factor.

source: Image A is 60 mm by 40 mm. Image D is 90 mm by 60 mm and ima
video_script.why: The child has seen that a copy keeps the shape with one factor on both sides; now the child names that as a proportional change and tests an enlargement.
video_script.substitution: Divide each new side by the old side, then compare the two factors; the same factor means the change is proportional.
video_script.anchor: the book's tiger pictures: image A, and the enlarged copies D and E
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees the width grow by thirty millimetres and the height grow by only twenty, and says image D is not proportional. Each side grew by half of itself, so the factors are the same and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Image D is image eigh enlarged by three halves on both sides, and image E is not.

final_answer.spoken: image D, with the factor three halves on both sides

hold_back: Answer: D is proportional to A
maths_rules: image A: 60 mm wide, 40 mm high
image D: 90 mm by 60 mm; 90 ÷ 60 = 3/2 and 60 ÷ 40 = 3/2; one factor 3/2, so proportional
image E: 60 mm by 60 mm; 60 ÷ 60 = 1 and 60 ÷ 40 = 3/2; 1 is not 3/2, so not proportional
Keeko's slip: 90 − 60 = 30 and 60 − 40 = 20 are different growths, but each is half of its old side: 1/2 × 60 = 30 and 1/2 × 40 = 20
video_script.design: One idea: the same factor on both sides is a proportional change. Assumes the factor of change from the last video. Wrong idea: different growth in length means not proportional. The three frames stay for the whole video.

narration: <bookmark mark='arrows'/>Each side of a copy comes from the old side by a factor of change.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>We find it by dividing the new side by the old side.
<bookmark mark='name'/>When the width and the height have the same factor, the change is called proportional.
<bookmark mark='tags'/>We need to compare the two factors.

<bookmark mark='diff'/>The two factors are different.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks image D is not proportional, because the width grew by thirty but the height by twenty.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>Ninety take away sixty is thirty, and sixty take away forty is twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the test is the factor, not the length that was added.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Each side grew by one half of itself, thirty for the width and twenty for the height.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Different growths can still come from the same factor.
